---
title: Filter-authored highlight spans
format: html
filters:
  - highlight-words.lua
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      dom-parity: true
      noErrors: true
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        # The filter produces `hl-error` and `hl-warning` spans around
        # the literal words ERROR and WARN. The HTML writer renders
        # them as nested <span class="hl-error"> and <span class="hl-warning">.
        # The container still carries `sourceCode log` — the walker
        # only skips the annotate step when `data-hl-spans` is already
        # present, not the sourceCode marking.
        - ["hl-error\">ERROR</span>",
           "hl-warning\">WARN</span>",
           "<pre class=\"sourceCode log\""]
---

Not every language you want to highlight has a tree-sitter grammar.
Quarto's highlighting is just an attribute on the AST — a
`data-hl-spans` key whose value is a JSON array of start/end/capture
triples — and any Lua filter (or JSON filter) can write that
attribute directly. The HTML writer handles the rest: nested
`<span class="hl-<capture>">` emission with dots becoming hyphens.

This document uses `highlight-words.lua` to highlight the literal
words `ERROR` and `WARN` in a fenced code block whose class is `log`
(not a registered language). Open the filter file to see the encoding
in about 30 lines of readable Lua.

```log
2026-04-20T10:12:01 ERROR connection refused
2026-04-20T10:12:04 WARN high latency detected
2026-04-20T10:12:09 ERROR timeout reading from upstream
```

The `hl-error` / `hl-warning` captures correspond to entries in the
default highlight SCSS theme. To use a completely new capture name,
ship your own CSS with `.hl-<your-capture> { … }` rules alongside the
filter.
